text:
alex: Heads up 1h run of kernel-routing + smaller batch-window landed on staging and we see host CPU up for short-rpc paths. p95 and p99 tail moved. anyone free to eyeball?

riley: on it. any traces? which metrics spike?

alex: uploaded a micro-trace + pprof to staging bucket. quick summary: ingress parsing doubled for many connections, and small write syscalls climbed. snippet below:
```
pprof top
ingress_router::route  34.2%  kernel_selector::route_by_fingerprint
ingress_proto::decode   21.5%  parse::decode_headers
net::socket::writev     11.3%  tcp::small_flush
tokenizer::tokenize      6.5%  pretoken::scan
```

devon: sounds like selector is re-parsing headers after routing. are we creating a new owned buffer path?

alex: yes - the new routing returns a "route + copy" which triggers owned-buffer validation in preparse. so effectively two parses + memcopy for small requests.

taylor: also noticed an HPACK/HTTP2 kicker if clients open short-lived streams. lots of header frames repeated. small frames == many writev calls. infra-bot shows small_write_rate up ~20%.

infra-bot: observed: small_write_rate +19% (1768602000-1768604300), connections short-lived ratio +14%, hpack_cpu per-call +16%.

riley: short term mitigation ideas: 1) memoize minimal parse (method, path, content-length) in selector and attach to request context; 2) add a 2ms per-connection coalesce for egress to fold headers+body; 3) try preserve-buffer-ownership route to skip copy.

devon: for 2) watch out for tail latency on long-lived streams. but for typical RPCs that return quickly, coalescing entries for 2ms is negligible and should reduce writev count.

alex: I prototyped selector memoization. locally it drops the duplicated parse. baseline p99=140ms; selector-memo p99=95ms for <=80 tokens.

taylor: great. question on rollout: selector memo changes routing metadata shape. could that shift keys across kvcache shards? we saw shard hotness change after last routing tweak.

riley: good call. we should snapshot kvcache key distribution before canary and compare. if routing moves >5% of top-10k keys we pause. also consider a grace window that pins existing shard mapping for hot prefixes during rollout.

devon: agree. small followup: implement memo as "minimal parse" not full parse object. include method, seq_len_hint, content_type. that keeps payload small and friendly to tracing.

alex: will update proto. also will add a canary flag route.selector_memo = true. start at 2% traffic.

taylor: i'll run HPACK replay tests to estimate coalescing effect. if we can collapse consecutive headers into one write per-request that'll cut small writes by ~40% on our test set.

infra-bot: scheduled jobs: hpack-replay (1768606000), kvcache-snapshot (1768606100) for canary readiness.

riley: timeline: today - land selector-memo PR + unit tests; tomorrow - 2% canary + kvcache snapshot; day after - enable 2ms egress coalesce on canary and measure. metrics: p95/p99 latency, small_write_rate, kvcache_miss_rate.

devon: also hooking up a quick buffer-ownership hint in selector: returns preserve_ownership=true for cases where input is already in owned buffer. cheap change and avoids memcpy in 60% of paths. add to Phase 1 tests.

alex: thanks all. creating ticket INF-6130 with links to traces and canary checklist. I'll post results here as we go.

riley: ping me when canary is up, i'll watch dashboards and kvcache histograms.

taylor: i'll deliver the HPACK replay numbers and a small patch for egress coalesce.

alex: closing for now. will reopen thread if anomalies. :rocket:
